observations.behavior: Removes the use of a passed `currentUserId` prop to filter and group loops; this dependency is removed from P1.F2.H4.
observations.posthog_connection: Changes shared presentation props for desktop UI. This could affect how users see their Loop workspace, but no implementation or test change supports tier 3.

observations.behavior: Passes only the data-layer loading state instead of combining it with an authentication-loading flag that was previously supplied by P1.F2.H5.
observations.posthog_connection: Simplifies the component's contract: the view now relies solely on its own loader rather than an auth-dependent one. No tier 3 benefit demonstrated without backend changes.

observations.behavior: Deletes the optional numeric ID parameter from the interface definition, removing the ability to pass user identity into the presentation layer.
observations.posthog_connection: Reduces coupling between LoopsListView and authenticated client. Tier 2 possible if tests show correct behavior under both logged-in and anonymous states, which are not shown here.

observations.limitations: Only frontend TypeScript and JSX hunks provided. The actual filtering and grouping implementation in P1.F2.H6 removes a conditional check, but we do not have corresponding production code or end-to-end assertions showing this does not break existing groupings. Tests were also changed (P1) but they reflect expected new behavior rather than regression checks for removed functionality. No tier 3 systemic change is established.

review.reason: The chunk demonstrates removal of an unnecessary dependency (`currentUserId`) and simplification of shared props and filters. This could improve reliability and reduce cognitive load, supporting a bounded improvement. However, no broader system-wide benefit or critical-path protection is demonstrated across components, so it cannot reach tier 3. It exceeds narrow maintenance because multiple related hunks change shared interfaces and behavior, not just comments or isolated lines.
review.posthog_relevance: Desktop workspace UI: changing how loops are grouped by visibility instead of ownership can affect discoverability and account switching; relevance depends on whether backend still supports that distinction and whether downstream consumers rely on `currentUserId`.
review.uncertainty: Without the complete component implementation and tests, I cannot verify that removing the ID-based filter preserves correct personal/team separation under all authentication states.
